items.title: Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1969-12-14
items.q: Miriam is mentioned only by the interviewer as a companion ('Miriam and I went out'). The interviewee, Johnny Wiggs, does not mention Miriam, nor does he respond to her name with any personal connection.

ctx.x: Yes, let me just. Some people make five dollars a shot at it.

Well, a long time ago, maybe, oh, fifteen or sixteen years ago, I was with a friend from the country area of Louisiana. He was actually from Farmerville up in Union Parish. And he came to New Orleans and, you know, he and his wife and Miriam and I went out. We went to a few of the places. And when they played the saints, when the saints go marching in, he said that he felt someday we would be sorry we jazzed up that song because it was a spiritual and a very sacred spiritual. And the song was being desecrated.…

this. I'm sorry. Very short two-word comment. I'm sorry. Okay. Have you ever heard this, Dick? Well, I hear people say that, and of course, different people have different feelings about it. Some jazz musicians feel that it's not sacrilegious at all to play a hymn, and I think people are very much concerned with their afterlife, and this isn't one attitude towards death, that you should rejoice at it and expect some future life. Many people don't feel that that's a wrong thing to do, to enjoy yourself that way.…
